subject: Urgent: Rivergate v5.1 quant rollout — throughput & p99 regression
messages:
From: Jessica Holt <jessica.holt@rivergate.com>
To: naomi_feldman@redwood.com
Cc: paul.nguyen@rivergate.com
Date: 2028-05-17T09:14:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Production spike after v5.1 deploy — urgent

Naomi / Redwood team,

We pushed v5.1 with the new INT8 quant profile to 100% at 04:30 PT and immediately started seeing p99 latency jump from ~420ms to >1.2s and a throughput collapse (5xx rate climbed from 0.2% to ~3.8%). This is affecting our checkout flow across all regions.

Attaching logs.zip and a short flamegraph from our SRE dashboard. We rolled traffic to a static fallback in the morning but we need a coordinated plan — this is customer-facing and leadership is asking for an update.

Please advise next steps and whether you can roll us back to the previous profile.

Thanks,
Jessica Holt
SRE Lead | Rivergate Inc

Subject: Re: Production spike after v5.1 deploy — urgent

Jessica — thanks for the quick flag. Sorry you’re seeing this in prod. We’ve stood up an incident call; I’ve looped in Ben (SE) and Rishi (SRE ops) who will lead triage. Immediate plan:

- Ben/Rishi will review the logs and traces you attached and run a memory + kernel profile against the v5.1 INT8 profile.
- If we confirm quant decode pressure is the root cause, we will execute a canary rollback for your production routes and route traffic to v5.0 while we investigate.
- I’ll set up a 30-minute sync at 10:00 PT; invite incoming.

We’ll escalate to the exec bridge if we cannot stabilize within 90 minutes. I’m reporting this to our CS and leadership now.

Naomi Feldman

(650) 555-0192

From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
To: naomi_feldman@redwood.com, Jessica Holt <jessica.holt@rivergate.com>
Cc: rishi_malhotra@redwood.com, irene_choi@redwood.com
Date: 2028-05-17T10:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Production spike after v5.1 deploy — urgent

Jessica / team — I pulled the logs quickly. First-pass findings:

- There are repeated decode stalls with large KV-cache churn immediately after the first generation tokens; memory allocs spike and we hit a GC-like stall in our runtime (see trace snippet below).
- The INT8 kernel path introduced a different attention kernel that performs slightly faster in steady-state, but in short-sequence, high-concurrency workloads it appears to create extra memcpy/zeroing overhead on our stack, pushing p99 up.
- Error traces in logs.zip show transient OOMs for a small percentage of requests, which explains the 5xx spike.

Immediate remediation options (ordered):
1) Canary rollback: take 10% of traffic off v5.1 to v5.0 for 15 minutes; if p99 drops and 5xx clears, expand rollback.
2) Route high-concurrency hotpaths (checkout) to the legacy modelpack (v5.0) as a targeted mitigation.
3) If rollback is not acceptable, we can apply a temporary runtime throttle that limits concurrency per-GPU and pre-warms KV cache for hot keys.

I’m preparing a minimal rollback plan and will push traces to the shared Drive.

—Ben
Ben Carter | Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference

- 10:30 PT: Executed a canary rollback on checkout routes (10% traffic) to v5.0; observed p99 drop from ~1.25s to ~430ms within 7 minutes and 5xx rate returned to baseline.
- 11:00 PT: Expanded rollback to 40% after validation; metrics improved globally.
- 12:15 PT: Rolledback to 100% for checkout while we continue investigation on v5.1 kernel path.

Attachments pushed: p99-trace.pdf (comparison traces) and rollback-plan.docx (detailed steps and smoke tests).

Next steps:
- Engineering (Rishi, Ben, Irene) will reproduce the issue on a staging fleet with our profiling flags and report a root-cause by EOD tomorrow.
- I’ll coordinate an executive briefing with Rivergate for 08:30 PT tomorrow to share impact, remediation, and compensation proposal.
- Marissa / CS will draft the customer incident note and credit proposal.

Jessica / Paul — thanks for partnering closely today. We’ll keep you updated realtime in the shared Drive and the incident channel.
